newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Jinro firms limit-up on plan to sell affiliates.
newsitem.headline: Jinro firms limit-up on plan to sell affiliates.

text.p: Shares in Jinro Ltd and two other listed units of the troubled Jinro Group rose to their upper daily limits in early Thursday trading after the group said it would sell most of its affiliates and real estate, brokers said.
Jinro rose 530 won to 7,180, Jinro Industries Co was up 370 won to 5,070 and Jinro General Foods Co up 320 won to 4,370.
"Jinro Group firms are under focus as investors believed the sales plan would help accelerate the group's self-rescue plan," said Koh Soon-shik of LG Securities.
The group, which was selected in April by its creditor banks for bailout, said on Thursday it would sell 12 of its 18 affiliates and real estate to generate 840 billion won.
Jinro, one of South Korea's oldest conglomerates and the nation's biggest maker of the traditional liquor "soju", has been struggling under mounting debt.
